S7 Class for Shape Constraints

Source: R/shape.R
shape_constraint.Rd

shape_constraint is the parent class of the shapes that scs() imposes on a smooth: shape_increasing(), shape_decreasing(), shape_convex() and shape_concave(). A shape writes the B-spline coefficients of the smooth as \(\beta = A\,b(\gamma)\), where \(A\) is a fixed matrix of cumulative sums on the Greville abscissae of the basis and \(b\) applies the inverse of a link to the constrained coordinates one at a time, so every free vector \(\gamma\) gives a curve of that shape.

Usage

shape_constraint(shape_name = character(0), link = NULL, shape_params = list())

ShapeMonotone(shape_name = character(0), link = NULL, shape_params = list())

ShapeCurvature(shape_name = character(0), link = NULL, shape_params = list())

Arguments

shape_name

A single string naming the shape.

link

A linkfunctions7 link onto \((0, \infty)\).

shape_params

A named list of the shape's own settings.

Value

An S7 object of class shape_constraint.

The map

With \(\xi_1 < \dots < \xi_K\) the Greville abscissae of a B-spline basis and \(h_j = \xi_{j+1} - \xi_j\), a monotone shape parametrizes the slopes \(s_j = (\beta_j - \beta_{j-1}) / h_{j-1}\) and a convex or concave shape the second divided differences of the coefficients. A B-spline whose coefficients have nonnegative slopes is nondecreasing, and one whose slopes on the Greville abscissae are nondecreasing is convex, which holds for any knot placement, including the knots repeated at the ends that basis7 uses.

On a constrained coordinate \(b_j = \ell_j + g^{-1}(\gamma_j)\), with \(g\) the link of the shape (a link onto \((0, \infty)\)) and \(\ell_j\) a lower bound (zero, or the minimum slope). On a free coordinate \(b_j = \gamma_j\). The derivatives of the map are therefore diagonal: \(\partial^k b_j / \partial \gamma_j^k = (g^{-1})^{(k)}(\gamma_j)\) and every mixed derivative is zero.

A new shape

A user-defined shape is a subclass of shape_constraint with methods for shape_map() and shape_start().

See also

scs(), shape_map(), shape_start().

Examples

sh <- shape_increasing()
S7::S7_inherits(sh, shape_constraint)
#> [1] TRUE
sh@shape_name
#> [1] "increasing"
